key_insight: Two-frequency cylinder oscillations break the symmetric steady-streaming pattern and can generate directional pumping, with the net force depending strongly on amplitude ratio and phase difference.
engineering_relevance: The result provides a tunable mechanism for microfluidic pumping, suggesting two-frequency actuation could be used to control flow in lab-on-a-chip and related devices.
method: Reduced the asymptotic steady-streaming problem on an annulus to a sequence of 1D boundary value problems.
Solved the reduced problems numerically to map force dependence on amplitude ratio, phase difference, and Reynolds number.
Validated the annulus proxy by comparing with full simulations of a two-frequency oscillating cylinder in a rectangular channel.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that for frequency ratio 2, the net force follows a simple scaling law in amplitude ratio and phase, and channel simulations show flux is directly proportional to annulus force across all tested parameter ranges.
watch_item: The annulus-to-channel force/flux relationship was tested over limited parameter ranges, so broader validity and device-specific implementation still need confirmation.
paper_title: Pumping by Two-frequency Steady Streaming: Impact of Amplitude Ratio and Phase
